statements.status_notes: Code injection via _.template imports key names. The advisory marks all lodash releases through 4.17.23 as vulnerable, with the only fix in lodash 4.18.0, which is deprecated by upstream as a bad release and introduces breaking changes in baseAssignValue/fromPairs that crash the webpack UI build (html-webpack-plugin _.template). The Argo CD UI is pinned to the newest non-broken release, 4.17.23, and does not pass attacker-controlled input to _.template imports. This will be patched once upstream ships a non-breaking fixed release.

Prototype pollution via array path bypass in lodash _.unset and _.omit. The only upstream release that includes the fix is lodash 4.18.0, which is deprecated by upstream as a bad release and introduces breaking changes in baseAssignValue/fromPairs that crash the webpack UI build (html-webpack-plugin _.template). The Argo CD UI is pinned to the newest non-broken release, 4.17.23. This will be patched once upstream ships a non-breaking fixed release.

Langfuse 2.x is end-of-life upstream (last release v2.95.12 on 2025-11-18; no further releases). Transitive dependencies are pinned by the upstream pnpm-lock.yaml or built into the migrate binary at compile time. The vulnerable code paths are not reachable through the entrypoint server.js — the npm tree is bundled by Next.js for the standalone runtime which does not invoke these libraries on hot paths. Customers requiring active CVE remediation should adopt the langfuse 3.x DHI variant; this v2 image is published for migration compatibility only.
